report_name: Levi Strauss & Co. Discloses Breach from Social Engineering Attack

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Social Engineering Actor
threat_actors.description: The unnamed third party that conducted a targeted social engineering attack against Levi Strauss & Co. employees, leading to the exfiltration of corporate data.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Attackers conducted a targeted social engineering campaign, manipulating three employees to gain initial access to their company-issued computers.

attack_patterns.name: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: The social engineering attack likely involved employees opening a weaponized document, leading to malware execution, as suggested by hunting hints for suspicious process chains originating from Microsoft Office applications.

attack_patterns.name: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: PowerShell was likely used for post-compromise activities, as hunting hints suggest monitoring for Microsoft Office applications spawning scripting engines like powershell.exe.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: A remote access trojan (RAT) or other malware was likely installed on compromised computers to maintain persistent access.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: Attackers collected an unspecified amount of corporate data from the compromised employee workstations.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The attackers exfiltrated collected corporate data from the compromised computers to their own servers.

attack_patterns.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack_patterns.description: Attackers likely used persistence mechanisms such as Registry Run Keys to maintain access to the compromised systems, as implied by the installation of a Remote Access Trojan.

identities.name: Levi Strauss & Co.
identities.description: Global apparel company that disclosed a data breach after three of its employees were targeted by a social engineering attack, resulting in the exfiltration of corporate data.

identities.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
identities.description: The regulatory agency with which Levi Strauss & Co. filed an 8-K form to disclose the cybersecurity incident.

infrastructure.name: Attacker C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Unknown command-and-control infrastructure used by the attackers to exfiltrate corporate data from compromised Levi Strauss & Co. workstations.

indicators.name: Suspicious Microsoft Office Process Chain
indicators.pattern:
title: Microsoft Office Product Spawning Script Interpreter
id: 2b8a1c3d-f4e5-4b6a-8c7d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects a Microsoft Office product spawning a script interpreter process (e.g., powershell.exe, cscript.exe), which is often indicative of a malicious document executing a payload.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/levi-strauss-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-09
tags:
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\WINWORD.EXE'
      - '\EXCEL.EXE'
      - '\POWERPNT.EXE'
      - '\OUTLOOK.EXE'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects a Microsoft Office application spawning a scripting engine, a common technique for executing malware from a malicious document, as mentioned in the report's hunting hints.

indicators.name: Suspicious Remote Access Tool Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Remote Access Tool Execution
id: 9d8c7b6a-5f4e-4d3c-2b1a-0e9f8d7c6b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of common remote access tools like AnyDesk or TeamViewer, which could indicate unauthorized remote access if run on non-IT workstations.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/levi-strauss-data-breach/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-09
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.command_and_control
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate use by IT support personnel.
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\AnyDesk.exe'
      - '\TeamViewer.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of common remote access tools, which the report identifies as a major red flag for compromise on non-IT employee computers.
